title: Intune Enrollment-Time Device Grouping — Prerequisites, Setup & Troubleshooting (Autopilot Device Preparation + Apple ADE)
author_notes: Effort tier: T3 (cross-platform enrollment diagnostic + setup; Graph/RBAC depth).

Intune/Entra admin center + Microsoft Graph authored at exact detail from Microsoft public docs. KEY FACT (field-validated): Enrollment-Time Grouping requires the Intune Provisioning Client first-party service principal (AppId f1346770-5b25-470b-88bd-d5744ab7952c, in some tenants displayed 'Intune Autopilot ConfidentialClient' — match by AppId, name varies) to be an OWNER of an ASSIGNED, cloud-only Security group; without it, saving the enrollment policy fails with 'Unable to save device group ... the Intune Provisioning Client application is not an owner'. Microsoft documents this for Windows Autopilot device preparation; Apple ADE exposes the same Device Group option and uses the same backend but is barely documented for Apple — cite that gap, do not invent Apple-specific Microsoft docs that don't exist. The Azure Activity Log AuthorizationFailed / microsoft.insights/eventtypes/values/read errors seen in the portal are an UNRELATED red herring (Azure Monitor Reader-access, not Intune). Version/preview-dependent (Enrollment Time Grouping is newer) — flag 'verify in your tenant'. Automation is PowerShell (Microsoft Graph). No client names, no real tenant/admin identifiers. No secrets in code.
hook: Fix the "Intune Provisioning Client is not an owner" enrollment-grouping failure — for Autopilot and Apple ADE
problem: You configure a device group on a Windows Autopilot device-preparation policy or an Apple ADE enrollment policy, it saves… and fails: "Unable to save device group … the Intune Provisioning Client application is not an owner." The group looks right, the policy is valid, yet Enrollment-Time Grouping won't commit — and the portal buries you in unrelated AuthorizationFailed Azure-log errors that send you chasing the wrong thing. This solution is the definitive prerequisites, setup, and diagnostic playbook: the exact group configuration, the required Intune Provisioning Client owner, the RBAC scope rules, and a symptom→root-cause tree that maps each error string to its real cause — so enrollment-time grouping saves and populates devices, on Windows and Apple.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — what Enrollment-Time Grouping is and the mechanism that trips everyone up: the Intune Provisioning Client service principal must own the assigned group so Intune can add devices at enrollment. Applies to Windows Autopilot device preparation AND Apple ADE (shared / no user affinity) — Microsoft documents it for Windows; Apple uses the same backend with little Apple-specific documentation.

Prerequisites Matrix — every requirement with how to verify/implement: Security group, Assigned membership (never Dynamic), Cloud-only (not synced from on-prem AD), not mail-enabled, not Entra-role-assignable, ideally empty, the Intune Provisioning Client as Owner (AppId f1346770-5b25-470b-88bd-d5744ab7952c), the admin able to manage the group, and the group inside the admin's Intune RBAC scope groups.

Setup Guide (both platforms) — create the group to spec, add the Intune Provisioning Client owner (match by AppId; provision the SP if absent), then wire it to a Windows Autopilot device-preparation policy and an Apple ADE enrollment-token policy — named steps, propagation waits, and validation.

Diagnostic Playbook — a symptom→root-cause decision tree: the generic "Updating device group for Apple enrollment policy" hang, the definitive "…Intune Provisioning Client application is not an owner" error, the Azure Activity Log AuthorizationFailed / microsoft.insights/eventtypes/values/read red herring (ignore it), propagation delay, SP-named-differently, SP-missing, RBAC-scope, and how to inspect the real backend error via Graph / browser dev tools before escalating to Microsoft.

5 PowerShell (Graph) tools — group-readiness assessment (type/membership/source/mail/role-assignable/owner), an add-owner remediation (-WhatIf), a full prereq + RBAC-scope validator, a diagnostic report that maps the observed error to its cause, and a scope/config helper — read-only or dry-run by default, no secrets in code.
short: The definitive fix for Intune Enrollment-Time Grouping failures — the Intune Provisioning Client must own an Assigned, cloud-only Security group, plus the full prerequisite matrix, RBAC-scope rules, and a symptom→root-cause tree (incl. the Azure-log red herring) — for Windows Autopilot device preparation AND Apple ADE. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
